## What The Business Is

Coherent Corp. is a global photonics and compound-semiconductor company serving communications, AI data centers, industrial lasers, instrumentation, electronics, and materials markets. The company describes itself as a “global photonics leader” with core capabilities in materials, optics, lasers, thermoelectrics, and networking products. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/company/about-us?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

Coherent makes optical components, transceivers, lasers, engineered materials, thermoelectric products, and photonic subsystems used to move, generate, shape, and manage light. Its current growth center is Datacenter & Communications: 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, ZR/ZR+ coherent modules, optical circuit switches, indium phosphide photonic devices, and co-packaged optics for AI data-center networks. It also sells industrial laser and materials products used in semiconductor equipment, manufacturing, medical, and scientific applications. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Coherent’s May 6, 2026 fiscal Q3 report showed record quarterly revenue of **$1.81 billion**, up **21% year over year**, with non-GAAP gross margin of **39.6%** and non-GAAP EPS of **$1.41**; management guided fiscal Q4 revenue to **$1.91 billion–$2.05 billion**. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/content/dam/coherent/site/en/documents/investors/financial-releases/2026/may-6/earnings-release-fy26-q3.pdf?utm_source=openai)) In the call excerpt, management said Datacenter & Communications represented **75%** of revenue, data-center revenue rose **37% year over year**, communications rose **60%**, backlog reached a record level, and orders extended into calendar 2028.

Capacity expansion is central to the bull case: management said 6-inch indium phosphide yields are exceeding legacy 3-inch lines and that internal InP capacity should double by calendar 2026, one quarter earlier than originally planned, then more than double again by the end of calendar 2027. On June 16, 2026, the U.S. Commerce Department announced a letter of intent for up to **$50 million** in CHIPS funding to expand Coherent’s Sherman, Texas 6-inch InP facility; Coherent said the project would double manufacturing space and quadruple wafer capacity. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/06/department-commerces-chips-program-announces-letter-intent-coherent-50?utm_source=openai))

NVIDIA’s recently announced strategic partnership remains a major validation signal. NVIDIA and Coherent announced a partnership to develop optics technology for next-generation data-center architecture, and the transcript notes a **$2 billion NVIDIA equity investment** plus a multiyear supply agreement extending through the end of the decade, covering CPO-related products including high-power continuous-wave lasers. ([nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-coherent-announce-strategic-partnership-to-develop-optics-technology-to-scale-next-generation-data-center-architecture?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Execution risk is high because the growth plan depends on rapid capacity ramps in constrained technologies. Management explicitly identified indium phosphide as an industry-wide bottleneck, and Reuters reported in June 2026 that China’s export restrictions on InP threaten AI data-center rollouts; the report said average 6-inch InP wafer prices had risen **250% to $5,000** since restrictions began. ([m.investing.com](https://m.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/chinas-control-over-indium-phosphide-exports-threatens-ai-data-centre-rollout-4736446?ampMode=1&utm_source=openai))

Capital intensity is rising. In fiscal Q3, Coherent’s capex increased to **$290 million** from **$154 million** in the prior quarter and **$112 million** a year earlier, and management said capex would increase sequentially again in fiscal Q4 to support data-center and communications demand. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/content/dam/coherent/site/en/documents/investors/financial-releases/2026/may-6/earnings-release-fy26-q3.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The business mix is increasingly tied to AI optical-networking adoption timelines. The transcript frames CPO, OCS, multi-rail, and thermal solutions as future growth vectors, but several are still ramping or expected to begin revenue contribution later, including multi-rail in first-half calendar 2027 and thermal products in second-half calendar 2027. Industrial also remains soft: management said Industrial revenue declined modestly sequentially and year over year, reflecting weakness in parts of the broader industrial market.

## Transcript Read — Long Case

- Revenue guide for Q4 implies ~13% sequential growth at midpoint, accelerating from 9% in Q3
- Record backlog with orders extending to 2028; bookings up substantially QoQ
- 6-inch InP ramp one quarter ahead of schedule, yields exceeding 3-inch, contributing to gross margin
- OCS production bottleneck resolved, ramping fast; market opportunity doubled to $4B
- CPO NVIDIA partnership with $2B investment; CPO revenue expected 2H CY26
- 1.6T transceiver ramp faster than initially expected
- Communications 60% YoY growth, multi-rail and thermal solutions new growth drivers
- Non-GAAP EPS $1.41 up 55% YoY; Q4 guide implies further acceleration
- Balance sheet strengthened with $3B cash and 0.5x leverage

Rationale: Accelerating revenue growth, record backlog and demand visibility to 2028, 6-inch InP ramp ahead of schedule and yielding cost benefits, new product cycles (1.6T, OCS, CPO) ramping, and NVIDIA partnership signaling strong customer adoption.

- InP is an industry-wide bottleneck and China export restrictions have driven 6-inch wafer prices up 250%; supply risk on the very input Coherent is scaling.
- Gross margin guide (~40%) only modestly above Q3 and below long-term targets; R&D as % of revenue rising.
- Industrial remains soft; the story is a single-thesis AI-optics bet.
- The stock has re-rated massively (3-yr mean market cap ~$19B vs. $61B today) — the NVIDIA partnership and 1.6T/CPO ramps are substantially priced in.

## Multiple Re-Rating
- **Current implied multiple:** $63,246.6M EV / -$538.2M TTM FCF = **-117.5x** (negative and economically meaningless — the market is pricing through the capex trough).
- **12-month forward multiple:** **175x EV/forward-FCF** — an intentionally high "optical" multiple because forward FCF will still be capex-suppressed.
- **Direction: EXPAND** (from a negative/meaningless print to a high positive multiple as FCF inflects).
- **Top drivers:** (1) FCF turning positive but still artificially depressed by a $1.5B+ capex wave, which justifies a high multiple relative to underlying earnings power (~$1.1B+ non-GAAP net income run-rate); (2) demand visibility to 2028 and the NVIDIA agreement supporting a premium AI-infrastructure valuation regime; (3) offset: much of the CPO/NVIDIA catalyst is already priced after the ~3x re-rating, so I cap the multiple well below what pure momentum extrapolation would give.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** Next-12-month revenue ~$8.4B (Q4 guide $1.98B annualizing with continued double-digit growth). Non-GAAP net income ~$1.1B; add back D&A (~$500M) and SBC (~$250M), subtract working-capital build (~$200M) → operating cash flow ~$1.65B. Capex ~$1.5–1.7B (rising sequentially per management). - **Forward EV:** $400M × 175 = **$70,000M**.
- **EV → market cap bridge:** current EV − market cap gap = $63,246.6M − $61,456.2M = $1,790.4M net debt; hold constant.
- **Forward market cap:** $70,000M − $1,790.4M ≈ **$68,210M** (~11% upside from $61,456M today — strong fundamentals, but the biggest catalysts are largely priced).

TTM FCF is negative (-$538M), so the current EV/FCF multiple is meaningless/negative, and the market is paying ~$61B market cap on an FCF-burning asset — pure forward-hope pricing. Capex is escalating with no committed peak, and China's InP export restrictions (wafer prices +250%) threaten the very ramp the bull case depends on. Gross margin guide (40%) is only modestly above Q3 and below long-term target; R&D is climbing as % of revenue. Several new vectors (multi-rail, thermal) don't contribute revenue until CY27. Much of the NVIDIA/CPO catalyst is already priced — the stock has re-rated massively (market cap mean over 3y was ~$19B vs ~$61B now, std 95% of mean). If AI capex digestion or execution slips, the FCF inflection gets pushed out and the multiple compresses hard.

## Multiple Re-Rating

- **Current implied multiple (EV/TTM FCF):** negative and non-meaningful (EV $63,246.6M / TTM FCF -$538.2M ≈ **-117.5x**). This cannot be used directly; I anchor on a normalized forward FCF instead.
- **Approach:** I forecast 12-month forward FCF turning positive as the capex wave crests and revenue scales, then apply a forward EV/FCF multiple appropriate for a high-growth photonics leader whose FCF is still depressed by investment.
- **Forward FCF estimate:** Revenue running ~$7.6–8B annualized by mid-CY27, net income scaling toward ~$900M–1B. Capex peaks and moderates as % of a larger revenue base, so FCF crosses to roughly **+$450M** on a trailing basis 12 months out (still suppressed relative to net income by ongoing heavy capex).
- **Forward multiple:** **~130x** forward FCF. Direction: **N/A on the raw current number (negative)** → operationally this is a **CONTRACTION** of the growth premium as FCF normalizes. As FCF turns positive and grows, the optical FCF multiple falls from meaningless/infinite toward a still-elevated but declining figure. Relative to the fully-priced AI narrative, I contract the premium.
- **Top drivers:** (1) FCF inflection from negative to positive as capex crests — mechanically collapses the optical multiple; (2) NVIDIA/CPO catalyst largely priced already, limiting further multiple expansion; (3) InP supply/geopolitical risk and modest gross-margin guide cap the re-rating ceiling.

## Logic

Current TTM FCF is negative, so I value off a normalized forward FCF of ~$450M reflecting the capex wave cresting while revenue continues to accelerate. TTM FCF is deeply negative at -$538M and worsening as quarterly capex escalates from $112M a year ago to $290M in Q3, with further sequential increases guided. China's InP export restrictions have driven 6-inch wafer prices up 250% to $5,000, threatening both cost structure and ramp timelines. Q4 gross margin guide of ~40% is only modestly above Q3 and below longer-term targets. Industrial segment remains soft. Several growth vectors (multi-rail, thermal, CPO) are still pre-revenue or early ramp, meaning near-term execution risk is concentrated. The stock has already re-rated massively — market cap of $61.5B is 3.2x the 3-year average of $19.2B — leaving little room for disappointment.

- **Current implied multiple:** -117.5x (negative/undefined — TTM FCF is -$538.2M)
- **12-month forward multiple:** 200x
- **Direction:** Contract
- **Drivers:**
  1. **Capex wave peaking into CY2027**: As InP capacity doubles by end of CY2026 and 1.6T/OCS ramps mature, capex intensity should begin moderating in the back half of the forward horizon, converting optical expansion into FCF normalization. The market will price the compression from "infinite" (negative FCF) toward a still-elevated but finite multiple as FCF turns positive.
  2. **Re-rating already largely priced**: At 3.2x historical average market cap, the NVIDIA partnership, CPO pipeline, and 1.6T ramp are extensively discounted. The second derivative of growth will naturally slow as the initial transceiver super-cycle annualizes, limiting further multiple expansion.
  3. **InP supply risk caps upside**: China export restrictions and 250% wafer price increases create cost pressure and ramp risk that markets will increasingly discount as the "supply-constrained growth" narrative matures.

**Forward FCF estimate: ~$300M.** TTM revenue of $6.6B should grow to ~$8.3–8.5B over the next 12 months given Q4 guidance of ~$2.0B and continued acceleration. With gross margins stabilizing around 40–41%, operating income should reach ~$1.7–1.9B. Operating cash flow, after working capital, should approximate $1.6–1.7B. Capex remains elevated at ~$1.2–1.4B annually as the InP expansion and CPO capacity build continue through CY2027, but should moderate somewhat from the current $290M+/quarter run rate as initial phases complete. Net FCF of ~$300M represents the inflection from deeply negative to modestly positive — the first step in normalization.

**Forward EV/FCF multiple of 200x** reflects a contraction from the current undefined/negative multiple. This is still an optically elevated multiple, justified by the ongoing capex wave that suppresses near-term FCF below its normalized run-rate (which could exceed $1.5B post-capex cycle). However, 200x rather than higher reflects that: (a) the stock has already re-rated 3x+ on exactly this thesis, (b) much of the CPO/NVIDIA/1.6T narrative is now consensus, and (c) InP supply risk introduces real execution friction. A normalized post-capex FCF of ~$1.5–2.0B in 2–3 years at a 30–40x terminal multiple implies a $45–80B future EV; 200x on $300M near-term FCF ($60B EV) sits in the lower-middle of that range, appropriately cautious.

**EV-to-MC bridge:** Current EV − MC gap = $63,246.6M − $61,456.2M = $1,790.4M (net debt). Forward EV = $300M × 200 = $60,000M. Forward MC = $60,000M − $1,790.4M = $58,209.6M ≈ $58,210M.
